questions.stem:
(a) Explain the concept of temperature. [2 marks]
(b) Name three types of thermometer and state the principle of each. [6 marks]
(c) Convert (i) -18 °C to kelvin, (ii) 77 °F to °C, (iii) 100 °F to degrees Rankine. [6 marks]
(d) State the triple point of water. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) degree of hotness or coldness of a body; determines direction of heat flow
2 marks: (b) liquid-in-glass: expansion of liquid
2 marks: (b) thermocouple: e.m.f. at junction of dissimilar metals
2 marks: (b) resistance thermometer: change of resistance with temperature (or gas thermometer: pressure change)
2 marks: (c)(i) -18 + 273 = 255 K
2 marks: (c)(ii) (77 - 32) x 5/9 = 25 °C
2 marks: (c)(iii) 100 + 459.67 = 559.67 °R
1 mark: (d) 0.01 °C
questions.explanation: -18 °C = 255 K; 77 °F = 25 °C; 100 °F = 559.67 °R. Triple point of water is 0.01 °C.

questions.stem:
(a) State Dalton's law of partial pressures. [2 marks]
(b) Refrigerant vapour at 180 kPa absolute and 17 °C occupies 0.09 m³. It is compressed to 0.03 m³ and its temperature rises to 77 °C. Calculate the final absolute pressure. [6 marks]
(c) If atmospheric pressure is 101 kPa, what will a gauge read? [2 marks]
(d) Name three pressure measuring instruments. [3 marks]
(e) Why is a compound gauge used on the suction side? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) total pressure of a gas mixture equals the sum of the partial pressures of its components
1 mark: (b) T1 = 290 K, T2 = 350 K
2 marks: (b) p2 = p1V1T2/(V2T1)
3 marks: (b) p2 = 180 x 0.09 x 350/(0.03 x 290) = 651.7 kPa
2 marks: (c) gauge = 651.7 - 101 = 550.7 kPa
3 marks: (d) any three: Bourdon tube gauge, manometer, barometer, compound gauge (1 each)
2 marks: (e) suction pressure may fall below atmospheric (vacuum), compound gauge reads both vacuum and pressure
questions.explanation: p2 = 180 x 0.09 x 350/(0.03 x 290) = 651.7 kPa absolute; gauge 550.7 kPa. Instruments: Bourdon gauge, manometer, barometer. Compound gauges read vacuum and pressure.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the operation of a thermostatic expansion valve. [6 marks]
(b) State four properties of a good refrigerant. [4 marks]
(c) Give the refrigerant number of (i) dichlorodifluoromethane, (ii) chlorodifluoromethane, (iii) carbon dioxide. [3 marks]
(d) Why is R-12 no longer used in new equipment? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) sensing bulb clamped to evaporator outlet senses suction line temperature
2 marks: (a) bulb pressure acts on diaphragm opening the valve against spring and evaporator pressure
2 marks: (a) valve opens more when superheat rises, closes when it falls, keeping superheat constant
4 marks: (b) any four: low boiling point, non-toxic, non-flammable, high latent heat, chemically stable, environmentally friendly, easy leak detection (1 each)
3 marks: (c) R-12, R-22, R-744 (1 each)
2 marks: (d) it is a CFC that depletes the ozone layer and was phased out under the Montreal Protocol
questions.explanation: TEV meters liquid to keep superheat constant via bulb, diaphragm and spring. Good refrigerants boil low, are safe, stable and have high latent heat. R-12, R-22, R-744. R-12 is an ozone-depleting CFC.

questions.stem:
For each of the following faults in a split air-conditioner, state one likely cause and one remedy:
(a) Indoor unit drips water into the room. [3 marks]
(b) Compressor runs but no cooling, suction pressure very low. [3 marks]
(c) Outdoor fan does not run, compressor trips after a short time. [3 marks]
(d) Ice forms on the indoor coil. [3 marks]
(e) Unit does not start at all, display blank. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) blocked/disconnected drain pipe or wrongly sloped unit; clear/re-route drain, level the unit
3 marks: (b) refrigerant leak/undercharge; locate leak, repair, evacuate and recharge
3 marks: (c) faulty fan capacitor or motor; test and replace capacitor/motor
3 marks: (d) dirty filter/low airflow or low charge; clean filter, check fan and charge
3 marks: (e) no power, blown fuse, faulty PCB/remote; check supply, fuse and board
questions.explanation: Leaks from blocked drains; poor cooling with low suction from undercharge; fan failure from capacitor; icing from dirty filters or low charge; dead unit from supply, fuse or board faults.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the working principle of a cold room. [4 marks]
(b) Describe five steps in installing a prefabricated cold room. [10 marks]
(c) What is the function of a door heater strip? [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) insulated enclosure whose air is cooled by evaporator unit (unit cooler) inside
2 marks: (a) condensing unit outside rejects heat; thermostat controls temperature; vapour barrier on warm side
2 marks: (b) prepare level floor with insulation and vapour barrier
2 marks: (b) erect insulated panels and fit door with seals
2 marks: (b) mount evaporator/unit cooler inside and condensing unit outside
2 marks: (b) run, braze, pressure-test and evacuate pipework; connect drain and electrics
2 marks: (b) charge refrigerant, set controls, run and check temperatures
1 mark: (c) prevents door gasket freezing to the frame
questions.explanation: A cold room is an insulated box cooled by an internal evaporator with an external condensing unit. Installation: floor, panels, door, units, piping and testing, charging and commissioning. Door heaters stop the seal freezing.

questions.stem:
A technician starts a repair business with ₦600,000 cash. She buys tools for ₦250,000, buys gas cylinders on credit from Coolgas Ltd for ₦80,000, and earns ₦150,000 cash from repairs.
(a) Calculate her closing cash balance. [3 marks]
(b) Prepare a simple balance sheet showing assets, liabilities and capital. [9 marks]
(c) State three principles of accounting. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) cash = 600,000 - 250,000 + 150,000 = ₦500,000
3 marks: (b) assets: tools ₦250,000, stock ₦80,000, cash ₦500,000; total ₦830,000
2 marks: (b) liabilities: creditor Coolgas ₦80,000
2 marks: (b) capital ₦600,000 + profit ₦150,000 = ₦750,000
2 marks: (b) capital + liabilities = ₦830,000 = total assets
3 marks: (c) any three: business entity, double entry/duality, going concern, consistency, prudence, accruals (1 each)
questions.explanation: Cash ₦500,000. Assets ₦830,000 = liabilities ₦80,000 + capital ₦750,000. Principles: entity, duality, going concern.
